en.title: Prime Partitions of a Digit String
en.description:
Split the entire digit string, keeping its original order, into several primes, where each segment has no leading zeros and each prime lies in 2..10⁶; count the number of ways modulo 10⁹+7. The upper bound 10⁶ is restored from the original snapshot, not the 10⁸ mistakenly written in the catalog.

The input/output protocol was compiled independently by this site; upstream solutions are not executed.
en.input: One line containing a digit string of length 1..100000 whose first digit is not 0.
en.output: Output the single integer required by the problem.
en.explanation: The answers to the three public examples are, in order: 3; 1; 1. All examples have been verified by independent small-scale enumeration or state search.
hints: Sieve the primes below one million; let dp[i] be the number of valid partitions of the first i characters, and extend from each nonzero starting position by at most 6 digits.
